subject: Pilot extension: partial refund vs. credit — options and next steps
messages:
From: Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@clearharbor.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on trial top-up vs partial refund

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at ClearHarbor is excited about the latency profile and the model variant suggestions. We're running into a timing issue with our pilot: due to scheduling delays on our side we won't complete the full evaluation within the original 30-day window.

Two procurement questions came up:
- Can we get a short extension (2 weeks) to finish the final integration tests?
- If we don't convert to a paid plan, is Redwood able to issue a partial refund for the unused portion of the pilot invoice, or do you only offer account credit that would apply to a future purchase?

We want to understand the tradeoffs. A refund helps our internal finance team, but a credit might be easier operationally on your side. Can you lay out what options you can offer and how fast we could get an amendment in place?

Also looping in procurement (procurement@clearharbor.com) for visibility.

Best,
Jamie Ortega
Director, Integrations
ClearHarbor Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@clearharbor.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on trial top-up vs partial refund

Hi Jamie — appreciate the heads up and totally understandable. We can do both paths but there are some constraints to be aware of. High level:

Option A — Two-week extension (no charge):
- We extend the active pilot window by 14 days at no extra charge.
- Any usage beyond the original cap will need pre-approval; otherwise we throttle to the existing cap.
- Benefit: keeps finance neutral for you; gives the team more time to validate.

Option B — Partial refund of unused days (invoice credit/refund):
- We can issue a credit equal to unused prepaid days (pro rata) if you decide not to convert and provide a short form request from procurement.
- Timing: credits applied to the Redwood account within 7–10 business days; refunds (ACH) require finance review and typically 10–15 business days.

Option C — Conversion incentive + credit swap:
- If you convert to a paid Dedicated or Hosted commitment within 30 days of pilot close we can apply a credit equal to 40% of the unused pilot value toward your first month + a 10% conversion discount on the first 3 months.
- This is our preferred path for customers ready to move to production — it reduces friction while giving ClearHarbor a clear cost advantage.

I've attached a short addendum draft (pilot_addendum_v1.pdf) that captures the extension and the mechanics for credits/refunds. Ben — looping you for any constraints on capacity guarantees if we do a straight extension.

Let me know which option procurement prefers and we'll generate the amendment and a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Quick note from the seat/ops side: we can absolutely do a 14-day no-cost extension with the following caveats and an optional alternative concession.

Caveats for straight extension:
- The pilot will remain on shared capacity. If ClearHarbor expects a spike we recommend enabling a temporary burst window (we can add 8 hours of priority capacity for testing).
- Extension does not change the existing data retention or snapshot schedule.

Alternative concession (if ClearHarbor is sensitive to finance timing):
- We can convert the unused pilot days into a one-time account credit equal to 50% of the unused value (applied within 7 business days).
- Or — if you convert within 30 days — we increase the credit to 60% and add a 15% discount on committed volume for month 1.

Operational ask: procurement will need the amendment and a short note stating which option (extension vs. credit vs. refund) they prefer. For refunds our finance team will request the original PO/Invoice and a signed request from procurement.

Priyom — if you can confirm whether any burst capacity is needed for the final tests, we'll include it in the addendum.

—Ben

If Redwood is unwilling to expedite, we'd accept Account Credit but would need the credit to be visible on an invoice/statement we can submit to our AP team. For the conversion incentive, procurement would like the conversion discount documented (percentage and qualifying timeframe) and the DocuSign-ready amendment.

Hi Jamie / Procurement team — thanks for the clarity. After checking with finance and ops, here's the agreed approach we can finalize today: 

1) Two-week no-cost extension: active immediately upon DocuSign of the addendum. We will enable a one-time 8-hour burst window on request during the extension period (raise with Priyom).
2) If ClearHarbor elects not to convert: Redwood will issue a refund for unused prepaid days. We will prioritize these refunds and target 8–10 business days from receipt of the signed refund request + original PO.
3) Conversion incentive: if ClearHarbor converts to a paid commitment within 30 days of pilot close, Redwood will apply a credit equal to 40% of unused pilot value toward month 1 and a 10% discount on committed spend for the first 3 months.

I've attached the addendum (amendment_docusign.pdf) and a one-page refund request template inside the PDF. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/clearharbor/amendment/3b2f

Next steps:
- Procurement: please sign the addendum via DocuSign (link above) to activate the extension.
- Priyom: I'll hand the burst-window request to you if they need it.
- Jamie: let me know if you'd like the 40% credit bumped to 50% (requires finance approval and a short justification).

Thanks all — happy to hop on a 15-min call if helpful.

Best,
